items.prompt: What is the central argument of the talk?
items.evidenceText: effective programmes combine planting with long-term maintenance and local data

options.text: Any large tree-planting campaign will cool a city.
options.rationale: The talk explicitly says large numbers do not automatically guarantee cooler streets.

options.text: Tree planting works best when design and maintenance are treated as infrastructure planning.
options.rationale: This combines the evidence about maintenance, local data and infrastructure.

options.text: Paved surfaces should be removed from every city.
options.rationale: The passage describes paved surfaces but does not recommend removing all of them.

items.prompt: Why might a tree-planting programme fail?
items.evidenceText: The species, the width of the pavement, and access to water all influence the result.

options.text: The choice of species and local conditions may be unsuitable.
options.rationale: The evidence names species, pavement width and water access as determining factors.

options.text: Trees always release too much water vapour.
options.rationale: Water vapour is presented as part of the cooling mechanism, not an inevitable problem.

items.prompt: Which option best paraphrases the final sentence?
items.evidenceText: treat urban trees as infrastructure rather than decoration

options.text: Plan and maintain trees as an essential urban system, not merely as visual improvement.
Choose decorative trees instead of expensive infrastructure.
Plant trees only beside existing infrastructure.
options.rationale: The sentence concerns how trees are managed, not where they must be planted.
